children: China's manufacturing activity expanded at a faster pace in August, according to a private gauge, extending its growth streak to nine months--the longest period of expansion in five years.
The RatingDog general manufacturing purchasing managers index rose to 51.5 in August from 50.9 in July, data released by S&P Global showed Tuesday.
The reading outperformed the official gauge, which ticked up to 49.8 from 49.2, both below the 50 mark that separates expansion from contraction.
Output, new orders and exports all expanded at faster rates last month, according to RatingDog. While purchasing and backlogs rose, employment didn't improve, it said.

The neutral employment reading for August "reflected a divergence across sectors, with consumer goods manufacturers adding staff, while intermediate and investment goods firms reduced headcount," according to Yao Yu, founder at RatingDog.
The accelerating rate of expansion for August exceeded the long-run series average, having also marked the fastest rise in new exports in six months, RatingDog said.
While business sentiment remained positive based on expectations of stronger market demand, overall confidence slipped to its weakest level since January.
